teams.heading: Fiji women secure inaugural WXV Challenger title after 20-17 victory over Netherlands
teams.body: The Fiji women's side secured the inaugural World Rugby WXV Global Series Challenger 2026 title following a 20-17 victory over the Netherlands in Hong Kong. A decisive kick in the 80th minute confirmed the win for Fijiana, who led 12-7 at half-time after tries from Merewairita Neivosa and Ivamere Nabura Rokowati. Despite severe heat delays that cancelled other tournament fixtures, Fiji finished top of the standings ahead of the Dutch and Spain, marking a significant achievement for the national women's programme.

teams.heading: England centre Benhard Janse van Rensburg stretchered off after heavy collision
teams.body: England centre Benhard Janse van Rensburg was stretchered off during Saturday’s Premiership clash between Bristol and Northampton. The incident occurred shortly before half-time following an awkward collision with Henry Pollock while attempting a tackle. The game at Ashton Gate faced an eight-minute stoppage as medical staff attended to the player. In the same fixture, Bristol’s Louis Rees-Zammit impressed with two tries, while Northampton’s Tommy Freeman struggled after being shifted into the full-back position.

teams.heading: Ireland women secure consecutive victories over Japan with seven tries
teams.body: The Ireland women's side secured a comprehensive 43-19 win over Japan in their Test match at Virgin Media Park in Cork on Saturday, scoring seven tries to claim consecutive victories following their previous win in Galway. Scott Bemand's side recovered from conceding an early try to build a 22-7 half-time advantage before extending their lead in the second period, with debuts off the bench marked by tries from Alana McInerney and Sophie Barrett as confidence grows ahead of their upcoming WXV fixtures in South Africa.

teams.heading: Hector Patterson attracts Bath attention amid potential England eligibility question
teams.body: Edinburgh scrum-half Hector Patterson has emerged as a transfer target for Bath ahead of next season as leading clubs monitor his contract situation. The 21-year-old, who represented Scotland at age-grade level and won the 2024 World Rugby U20 Trophy, is contracted only until the end of the campaign. Although he came through the Scottish system, Patterson is also eligible to represent England through a grandparent, leaving his international future open before he is capped at senior level.

teams.heading: Elliot Dee scores twice as Dragons defeat Scarlets in derby
teams.body: The Dragons secured a 36-26 victory over the Scarlets in a high-scoring United Rugby Championship encounter at Rodney Parade. Elliot Dee led the hosts with a brace as the Dragons outscored their rivals by six tries to four, with Anzelo Tuitavuki, Rodrigo Martinez, Huw Anderson and Robert Hunt also crossing. Macs Page scored twice for the Scarlets alongside tries from Sam O'Connor and Ioan Jones, while Scarlets captain Josh Macleod received a yellow card in the 68th minute.

teams.heading: Japan women's team suffer comprehensive forty-three to nineteen defeat against Ireland
teams.body: The Japan women's national rugby team fell to a 43-19 defeat against Ireland at Virgin Media Park in Cork on Saturday. Toshizumi Kitagawa's side struggled early as Ireland crossed the whitewash four times in the first half to establish a 22-7 advantage at the break. Despite tries from Sakurako Korai, Nami Asari and Nijiho Nagata, the visitors were unable to halt the hosts, who secured seven tries in total to wrap up consecutive wins in the series.

teams.heading: All Blacks captain Ardie Savea confirms move to the Blues
teams.body: All Blacks skipper Ardie Savea has signed with the Blues for the 2027 Super Rugby Pacific season. The 32-year-old loose forward will return to New Zealand rugby following his latest sabbatical with the Kobe Steelers in Japan, having previously represented Moana Pasifika in 2025. Savea said the club had 'always been on my heart' as he prepares to link up with the Auckland-based team later this year.

teams.heading: Stormers suffer Edinburgh defeat following Andre-Hugo Venter injury blow
teams.body: The Stormers dropped a 17-13 United Rugby Championship result against Edinburgh at Hive Stadium after losing hooker Andre-Hugo Venter to a head clash in the 22nd minute. Venter failed his head injury assessment, leaving John Dobson's side to win just 57% of their 21 lineout throws. Despite tries from replacement back Wandisile Simelane — later overturned for touch — and Man of the Match Hacjivah Dayimani, late lineout errors cost the visitors the match.
